question: What is the main goal of doing a general physical examination on a patient?

options.A: To establish a baseline overview of health status
options.B: To immediately prescribe definitive medical treatment
options.D: To discharge the patient from the hospital

explanation: Think of this as taking a snapshot of your patient's normal state. It gives you a starting point so you can easily spot and track any changes later on! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses do a quick general survey before diving into a detailed check of specific body systems?

options.A: It helps form an overall impression and guides further focus
options.B: It satisfies administrative paperwork requirements for admission
options.C: It allows the nurse to diagnose complex diseases instantly
options.D: It replaces the need to review the patient's medical chart

explanation: A quick look-over helps you catch any obvious signs of distress right away, telling you where you need to look closest during your exam. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which environmental setup is most important before you begin a physical exam?

options.B: An open door facing a busy hallway

explanation: Good lighting helps you see skin changes clearly, and privacy screens help your patient feel secure and respected. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the best way to help a nervous patient feel at ease before an exam?

options.A: Perform all painful procedures without warning
options.B: Ask family members to leave the room immediately
options.C: Avoid speaking to the patient to save time
options.D: Explain each step and obtain verbal consent first

explanation: Communication is key! Telling your patient what to expect builds trust, calms their nerves, and helps them relax. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the single most effective way to prevent passing infections between patients?
explanation: Good old handwashing is your superpower! It washes away germs picked up from patients and surfaces before they can spread. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: What must you do with your stethoscope before using it on a new patient?

options.A: Blow air through the tubing to clear dust
options.B: Warm the metal piece in hot water for five minutes
options.C: Wrap it tightly in gauze to keep it clean
options.D: Clean the diaphragm with an approved disinfectant wipe

explanation: A quick wipe down prevents you from accidentally carrying germs from one patient to the next. Safety first! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h3)

question: When doing a general survey, what are you mainly looking at?

options.A: Detailed function of the renal system
options.B: Exact chemical composition of the blood

explanation: You are taking in the big picture—how they look, how they move, and if they seem comfortable or in distress. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: You notice a patient is slurring their words and having trouble keeping their balance. Where do you log these observations?
explanation: Things like speech, posture, and balance are classic first impressions that belong right in your general survey notes. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h4)

question: Which assessment is so crucial that nurses often call it the 'fifth vital sign'?
explanation: Just like temperature and pulse, checking a patient's pain level helps you keep them comfortable and advocate for quick relief. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why do nurses measure vital signs during a physical checkup?

options.A: To check if the patient can walk unassisted
options.B: To quantify basic body functions and detect instability
options.C: To calculate the total cost of hospital admission
options.D: To determine the patient's exact religious beliefs

explanation: Vital signs give you hard numbers on how well the body's major systems are holding up, helping you catch trouble early. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: What is the correct order of techniques for a standard physical examination?
explanation: Remember the flow: Look first (inspection), feel gently (palpation), tap (percussion), and listen last (auscultation). Except for the belly! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: Why should you listen with your stethoscope (auscultation) before pressing on the belly (palpation) during an abdominal exam?

options.A: Palpation can alter natural bowel sounds
options.B: It shortens the total assessment duration
options.D: Auscultation warms up the abdominal wall

explanation: Pressing on the tummy can wake up the intestines and make them rumble more, so you want to listen to natural sounds first! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h6)

question: How should you write up your physical assessment findings in a patient's chart?
explanation: Stick to the clear facts and measurements you observed rather than guessing or using vague terms. Clear notes keep the whole care team safe! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)

question: What is your best immediate action if you discover a critical abnormality during your patient assessment?

options.A: Ask another patient for their opinion on the result
options.B: Delete the entry from the chart to prevent panic
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to write a report
options.D: Report the finding promptly to the healthcare team

explanation: Never sit on urgent findings! Quick communication ensures the patient gets the medical help they need right away. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h7)
